headline: The US Navy and the defence startup Shield AI are putting a further $300 million into X-BAT, a drone designed to take off and land vertically and fly itself in combat.
score_reason: New on 8 Oct; sizeable US military funding, but the aircraft has not flown and figures are company claims.
importance_line: The US Navy is backing AI-piloted combat aircraft that could fly from smaller ships, a possible change in how long-range strikes are carried out; the aircraft has not yet flown, and its specifications come from the company.
summary: Breaking Defense reports that the Navy approved a $150 million change to an existing agreement and Shield AI is matching it with $150 million of its own money, bringing the combined investment in the X-BAT drone to $400 million, with flight testing slated for later this year. Shield AI describes it as the "world's first AI-piloted VTOL fighter jet" with a range of more than 2,000 nautical miles, claims that have not been tested in flight; the Navy wants a drone that can launch from ships without large flight decks.
